title: Information-Theoretic Design of Sparse Autoencoder-Based Steering
abstract: arXiv:2611.01378v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Sparse autoencoder (SAE)-based activation steering is a lightweight approach for modifying the behavior of large language models (LLMs) by adding small vectors to hidden states during inference. However, designing effective steering interventions remains challenging. In this work, we develop an information-theoretic framework for analyzing SAE activations through empirical feature-firing distributions. The central object of the framework is the Jensen--Shannon divergence (JSD) between such firing distributions, which quantifies how far a generated or intervened state deviates from a dataset-induced target distribution. Based on an analytic divergence response for virtually shifted states, we construct steering vectors toward the target firing distribution. translated_title: 基于稀疏自编码器转向的信息论设计
translated_abstract: 基于稀疏自编码器（SAE）的激活转向是一种轻量级方法，通过在推理过程中向隐藏状态添加小向量来修改大语言模型（LLM）的行为。然而，设计有效的转向干预仍然具有挑战性。在这项工作中，我们开发了一个信息论框架，通过经验特征触发分布来分析SAE激活。该框架的核心对象是这些触发分布之间的Jensen-Shannon散度（JSD），它量化了生成或干预状态偏离由数据集诱导的目标分布的程度。基于虚拟移位状态的解析散度响应，我们构建了朝向目标触发分布的转向向量。同样的散度还可用于监测与另一个经验分布（例如通用的有效语言分布）之间的偏差。我们展示了该转向方法的有效性……（摘要原文在此处被截断）
tldr: 该论文提出了一个信息论框架，利用经验特征触发分布之间的Jensen-Shannon散度来分析SAE激活并构建有效的转向向量，从而更系统地设计对大语言模型行为的干预。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes an information-theoretic framework that uses Jensen-Shannon divergence between empirical feature-firing distributions to analyze SAE activations and construct effective steering vectors for intervening in LLM behavior.
